710566.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *pnew- Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥ Proto-Indo-European *pnéwmn̥ Proto-Hellenic *pnéumə Ancient Greek πνεῦμα From Proto-Hellenic *pnéumə, from Proto-Indo-European *pnéwmn̥, from *pnew-.

710529.t: Probably formed innovatively from πλήθω (plḗthō, “to fill”) + -ος (-os). Compare the relationship between πλῆθος (plêthos) ~ πλήθω (plḗthō) ~ πέπληθα (péplētha) and βριθύς (brithús, “heavy”) ~ βρίθω (bríthō) ~ βέβριθα (bébritha).

710532.t: From Proto-Hellenic *plḗtʰō, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- with root extension like plebs. Cognates include Latin pleo, Sanskrit पिपर्ति (piparti, “to fill”) and Avestan 𐬵𐬀𐬨𐬞𐬁𐬟𐬭𐬁𐬌𐬙𐬌 (hampāfrāⁱti).

710571.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pnew- (“to breathe, sneeze”). Cognates include Old English fnēosan (English sneeze).

710582.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷoiwéyō, as shown by Doric/Aeolic ποιϝέω (poiwéō), perhaps derived from a noun *ποιϝός (*poiwós) (seen in many compounds as the suffix -ποιός (-poiós)), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷoywós, from *kʷey- (“to pile, stow, gather”).

710541.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- (“to fill”). See also πίμπλημι (pĭ́mplēmĭ, “to fill”).

710596.t: From Proto-Hellenic *poimḗn, from Proto-Indo-European *poh₂imḗn, an abstract agent noun formed from an ablaut of *peh₂- (“to protect”) + *-mḗn.

710563.t: From the root of πλέω (pléō, “to float, sail”) (perhaps in some early meaning of "flow" > "abound") with the suffix -τος (-tos); for the suffix, compare βίοτος (bíotos, “life”), νόστος (nóstos, “journey, return”).

710526.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pléwō, from Proto-Indo-European *plew- (“to sail, flow”). In the present and imperfect, the semivowel *ϝ is lost between vowels, but before a consonant is kept as υ, the second element of a diphthong.

710530.t: Causative of πληθύω (plēthúō) with suffix -ύνω (-ū́nō), from πληθύς (plēthús, “throng”), from πίμπλημι (pímplēmĭ, “I fill”).

710531.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- (“to fill”) and closely related to Latin plēbs, though the exact pre-form of the term is unclear.

710550.t: From Proto-Hellenic *plā́t͏̌t͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *pl(e)h₂kyeti, from *pleh₂k-, *pleh₂g- (“to strike”).

710515.t: From Proto-Hellenic *plékō, from Proto-Indo-European *pleḱ-. Cognate with Latin plectō (“to plait, weave, twist”).

710503.t: Possibly from Proto-Hellenic *plát͏̌t͏̌ō, from earlier *plátʰyō, of uncertain origin.

710569.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *plew- Proto-Indo-European *-mṓ Proto-Indo-European *pléwmō Ancient Greek πλεύμων (pleúmōn) ▲ Ancient Greek πνέω (pnéō)influ. ▲ Ancient Greek πνεῦμα (pneûma)influ.

710507.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pléth₂os (“breadth”). Cognates include Sanskrit प्रथस् (práthas), Avestan 𐬟𐬭𐬀𐬚𐬀𐬵 (fraθah), Old Armenian լայն (layn), Welsh lled.

710580.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷos (“which”) + -θεν (-then, ablative adverb suffix). Compare its indefinite form ποθέν (pothén).

710599.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷos + -ιος (-ĭos, adjective suffix). Compare the indefinite form ποιός (poiós).

710527.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *pel- Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂g- Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂ Proto-Indo-European *pl(e)h₂géh₂ Proto-Hellenic *plāgā́ Ancient Greek πληγή From Proto-Hellenic *plāgā́, from Proto-Indo-European *pl(e)h₂géh₂, from *pleh₂g-,…

710589.t: From earlier *ποικιλός (*poikilós), with retraction of the accent by Wheeler's law; from Proto-Indo-European *peyḱ- (“to mark, embroider, color, paint”) + -λός (-lós).

710516.t: From πλέον (pléon, “too much”) + -άζω (-ázō, denominative verb suffix).

710514.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- Proto-Indo-European *-yōs Proto-Indo-European *pléh₁yōs Proto-Hellenic *pleíhōn Ancient Greek πλείων From Proto-Hellenic *pleíhōn, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁is-ō.

710505.t: Traditionally derived from πλατύς (plătŭ́s, “broad; flat”), or taken to be inherited directly from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥th₂enós (“wide; broad”), under the assumption that the tree was named after its broad leaves or flat patches of bark.

710544.t: From πληρόω (plēróō, “to fill”) + -μα (-mă, result noun suffix).

710556.t: From the o-grade of the root of πλέω (pléō, “to sail”) + -ιον (-ion), or inherited directly from Proto-Indo-European *plówyom (“floating vessel”): compare Proto-Germanic *flawją (“ship, vessel”).

710513.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁-der. Proto-Indo-European *polh₁ús Ancient Greek πολύς (polús) Proto-Indo-European *-yōsder.

710554.t: According to Beekes, the semantic field of architecture, as well as the presence of the element "-ινθ-", suggest a loan from Pre-Greek.

710547.t: Adverbial use of declination of πλησίος (plēsíos).

710546.t: From πλησίον (plēsíon, “near”) + -άζω (-ắzō, “suffix for verbs”). Compare cognate πελάζω (pelázō) and old πιλνάω (pilnáō).

710575.t: From Proto-Hellenic *póiwā, from Proto-Indo-European *póyH-weh₂, from *peyH-. Cognate with Lithuanian pieva (“meadow”).

710501.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pləks, probably from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”), sharing cognates with several Germanic languages through Proto-Germanic *flaką (“something flat”), *flakaz (“flat”); more at English flake.

710573.t: No clear etymology. Earlier attempts to analyze the formation as a conflation of several different verbs are unconvincing.

710564.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pluňňō, from a nasal-present formation of Proto-Indo-European *plew- (“to wash”), the same root of Latin pluit (“it rains”) and Old Armenian լուանամ (luanam, “to wash”).

710548.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pelh₂- (“to approach”). By surface analysis, an adjectival formation from πέλας (pélas, “near, nearby”).

710594.t: From the root of ποιμήν (poimḗn, “shepherd”) + -αίνω (-aínō), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to protect, shepherd”). Compare Latin pāscō (“to tend, feed, nourish”), Late Latin pāscor (“to feed onself, eat; pasture, graze”).

710504.t: The etymological base of the word is not clear. Formally, there is no reason to disconnect the word from πλάσσω (plássō, “to knead, mold”), but this linkage is not evident on the semantic side.

710565.t: Verbal adjective, from πλώω (plṓō, “to sail, float”) + -τός (-tós).

710577.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pṓds. Cognates include Mycenaean Greek 𐀡 (po) (dat. 𐀡𐀆 (po-de /⁠podei⁠/)), Latin pēs, Sanskrit पद् (pad), Old Armenian ոտն (otn) and հետ (het), Gothic 𐍆𐍉𐍄𐌿𐍃 (fōtus) and Old English fōt (English foot).

710597.t: From the root of ποιμήν (poimḗn, “shepherd”) + -η (-ē), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to protect, shepherd”).

710522.t: From πλέων (pléōn, “more”) + ἑκ- (hek-) (the root of ἔχω (ékhō, “to have”) + -της (-tēs).

710542.t: From πλήρης (plḗrēs, “full, complete”) + φορέω (phoréō, “to bear, wear”).
